lines.text: This is what you see. And this is what your car sees. Right now, they match.
Cameras need contrast. Rain cuts it. Fog erases it. The boxes flicker, and cars drop off the list.
LiDAR fires laser pulses and times the echo. But every water droplet sends back an echo too. The pulse returns early, and the points scatter.
Tests show fog hurts LiDAR more than rain does. In one fog chamber, detection dropped by half.
And just like that, the car is blind.
So how do engineers fix it?
First, radar. Its waves pass through fog with almost no loss.
Second, lasers at fifteen fifty nanometers. Eye safety rules allow more power, so more signal survives.
Third, thermal cameras. They read heat, not light, so warm bodies still stand out.
And coatings, air puffers, and wipers keep every lens clear.
No single sensor decides. The car blends them all. When one goes blind, the others cover.
